from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are arrows with magnitude and direction.",
            "Scalar multiplication stretches or shrinks a vector.",
            "Vector addition combines vectors via the parallelogram rule."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2 + UP*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        label = Text("v", font_size=24, color=WHITE)

        self.place_at_grid(vec, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'C4')
        self.place_at_grid(tip_glow, 'C3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(Create(vec), Write(label), FadeIn(tip_glow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#98FB98"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations and Span", [
            "Linear combinations sum multiple scaled vectors.", 
            "Span is the set of all reachable points.", 
            "Two non-collinear vectors span the whole plane."
        ])
        
        # Define vectors
        v = Vector([1, 1], color="#33FF57")
        w = Vector([2, -1], color="#33FF57")
        
        # Start vectors at origin in grid area (B2-C4)
        origin = self.grid["C3"]
        v.shift(origin)
        w.shift(origin)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(Create(v), Create(w))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33FF57")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        scalar = ValueTracker(1.0)
        v_scaled = always_redraw(lambda: Vector([scalar.get_value() * 1, scalar.get_value() * 1], color="#3357FF").shift(origin))
        self.add(v_scaled)
        self.play(scalar.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3357FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        v_plus_w = Vector([1+2, 1-1], color=WHITE).shift(origin)
        self.play(Create(v_plus_w))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Dependence means one vector is redundant.", "Redundant vectors lie on the existing span.", "Dependent vectors add no new reachable space."]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Rule", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define vectors
        v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, [1, 1, 0], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, [1.5, -0.5, 0], color=GREEN)
        v3 = Arrow(ORIGIN, [2.5, 0.5, 0], color=YELLOW) # v1 + v2
        
        # Initially add them
        vectors = VGroup(v1, v2, v3)
        self.place_at_grid(vectors, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display three vectors where one is a sum. (Color: #FF33FF)
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2), Create(v3), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF33FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash the redundant vector to highlight dependency. (Color: #FF0000)
        self.play(Flash(v3.get_end(), color=RED, line_length=0.2), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out the redundant vector to show subspace. (Color: #808080)
        self.play(FadeOut(v3), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#808080"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A basis is a minimal spanning set.", "Basis vectors are always linearly independent.", "Basis provides an efficient coordinate system."]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Basis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup vectors i and j
        i_vec = Vector(RIGHT, color="#00FFFF")
        j_vec = Vector(UP, color="#00FFFF")
        i_label = MathTex(r"\vec{i}", color="#00FFFF").next_to(i_vec, DOWN)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\vec{j}", color="#00FFFF").next_to(j_vec, LEFT)
        basis = VGroup(i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)
        self.place_at_grid(basis, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Square
        square = Square(side_length=1.0, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.2)
        square.move_to(basis.get_center() + np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0]))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(i_vec), Write(i_label), Create(j_vec), Write(j_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(square))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(square.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Combinations build spans.",
            "Dependence reveals redundancy.",
            "Removing redundancy leaves a basis."
        ])

        # Objects
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2]).scale(0.5)
        basis_i = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color=RED).add_tip()
        basis_j = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color=GREEN).add_tip()
        basis_k = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=OUT, color=BLUE).add_tip()
        basis_group = VGroup(axes, basis_i, basis_j, basis_k)
        
        summary_text = Text("Linear Algebra Foundations", font_size=32, color="#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(basis_group, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Create(basis_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.place_at_grid(summary_text, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(basis_group, scale_factor=1.2, color="#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Span to Basis

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows
sections.content: Briefly define a vector as an arrow in 2D space with magnitude and direction. Introduce scalar multiplication (stretching) and vector addition (the parallelogram rule) as the fundamental building blocks.
sections.example: Visualizing a drone moving 2 units East and 3 units North as a vector (2,3).

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Explain that a linear combination is the sum of scaled vectors. Define 'Span' as the set of all possible points reachable by scaling and adding a set of vectors. Use an animation showing the tip of the vector moving across the plane.
sections.example: Using two vectors v1=(1,0) and v2=(0,1), show that every point (x,y) in 2D space can be reached, meaning the span is the entire 2D plane.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Rule
sections.content: Explain that linear dependence occurs when at least one vector in a set is 'redundant'—it can be formed by a combination of the others. Visually show a third vector lying on the line formed by two others, adding no new 'reach'.
sections.example: Two robots moving; if Robot B just follows Robot A's path exactly, Robot B adds no new capability to the system.

sections.title: Defining the Basis
sections.content: Define a 'Basis' as the minimal set of vectors that spans the entire space without any redundancy (linearly independent). Emphasize that a basis is the 'efficient coordinate system' for a space.
sections.example: Comparing a 2D map using 3 vectors (redundant) versus 2 vectors (a basis); the basis is the 'perfect' set of directions to describe any location.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Review the progression: Linear combinations build a span; if the span is redundant, it's linearly dependent; remove the redundancy, and you find the basis. Connect this to the concept of 'dimension'.
sections.example: Visualizing a 3D coordinate system (x, y, z) as the 'basis' for a digital 3D game environment.
